text: Chair, Seth Lay, the Planning Development Department. The proposed substitute removes one section from the site plan applicability section in the that was proposed to be added by the Planning Commission. That section in the applicability section of the site plan says that existing nonconforming agricultural uses are exempt from site plan, which is actually generally true of all existing uses. They're all exempt from site plans. And we take the intent of that language and put it into the nonconformances section, which is where we talk about grandfathered uses. And we add language to that section in every subsection of the nonconforming uses section to clarify that nonconforming buildings are allowed to continue if they're annexed to the city, nonconforming uses are allowed to continue when they're annexed to the city, and nonconforming site conditions are allowed to continue when annexed to the city. Right now, the Unified Development Code only says uses that were approved prior to the adoption of the UDC receive nonconforming status. So if a property in the county was developed post 2012 met all county requirements, they could be nonconforming when they are annexed into the city. And so this section would allow those annexed properties to continue as nonconforming once they're annexed to the city, if they were legally established in the county.

text: afternoon, Mr. Chairman, members of city council. My name is Robin Lachin and I'm the city treasur. The resolution before you authorizes the write- off of approximately 74,700 in uncollectible accounts. Of that amount, approximately is city accounts. 11,500 is for BO poo sanitation accounts and the remaining 40,100 is for park unpaid parking tickets that were issued back in 2022. Each year, my office submits accounts to the governing body for write- off when they are more than four years old and collection efforts have been unsuccessful. We also include debts involving deceased individuals with no estate as well as debts discharged in bankruptcy. These accounts have gone through our collection process, but we've been unsuccessful in collecting the outstanding balances. I also want to mention that we recently submitted all past due parking tickets issued before June 30th to our collection agency, Professional Finance Company. They will begin collecting efforts within the next few days. One thing I want to emphasize is writing off these accounts does not mean we are forgiving the debt. Collection efforts will continue on debts that are remain legally collectible until the applicable statute of limitations extends. This is something we do each year to clean up our accounts and ensure that the financial records accurately reflect what we realistically expect to collect. And I'd be happy to answer any questions. Thank you.
